title: Pathogen Profiles
description: Multi-pathogen profile definitions for concurrent simulation in Crusher-to-the-Bridge.

EffectRange.description: [lo, hi] bounds a phenotype mutation's effect is drawn from.

decay_rate_per_day.description: Daily fraction of viable food-reservoir mass lost.

spore_decay_rate_per_day.description: Daily fraction of environmental spore mass lost.

StrainEvolution.description: Optional heritable-strain parameters (variant surveillance, Paper 3). Absent block = no strain structure for this pathogen.

mutation_rate.description: Probability of a point mutation per transmission event.

phenotype_mutation_fraction.description: Fraction of mutations that alter phenotype rather than only the neutral label.

within_host_mutation_rate.description: Probability of a point mutation per infected-agent-epoch. Default 0 keeps the transmission-only model as the baseline.

within_host_mutation_rate_per_day.description: Daily-authored probability of a point mutation per infected-agent day.

recombination_rate.description: Probability of a recombination event per co-infected agent-epoch.

recombination_rate_per_day.description: Daily-authored probability of a recombination event per co-infected-agent day.

superinfection_susceptibility.description: Relative susceptibility of an already-infected host to a second strain of the same pathogen (0 = complete homotypic interference).

prior_genotype_distribution.description: Weights over genotypes for pre-existing immunity in baseline immune agents. Renormalized on load; keys must be declared genotypes.

cross_immunity.description: Matrix [prior_genotype][challenge_genotype] = protection in [0,1]. Keys must be declared genotypes.

effect_ranges.description: Ranges phenotype mutation effects are drawn from.

min_strain_fraction.description: Frequency floor below which strains are lumped into an unresolved bin, bounding state growth.

immune_waning.description: How protection from a resolved exposure ages, per pathogen. cross_immunity says how well a prior exposure matches a challenge; this says how fresh it is. All times are days of natural history, converted from epochs through the run's clock. Absent block = no refractory window and no waning, i.e. the matched cross_immunity value applies at any age.

refractory_days.description: Days after an exposure resolves during which refractory_protection applies regardless of genotype match. Sized so re-infection within a week-long voyage is rare; the waning term below is what a year-long deployment sees.

refractory_protection.description: Protection inside the refractory window, breached in proportion to a challenge strain's immune_escape. 1.0 = sterile against a non-escaping challenge.

half_life_days.description: Half-life of the genotype-matched protection after the refractory window. 0 = no waning.

residual_protection.description: Floor the decay approaches, capped at the matched protection itself.

notes.description: Provenance for these rates: literature anchor, or the fact that a value is a placeholder pending one.

SequencingAssay.description: Optional clinical amplicon typing assay (variant surveillance, Paper 3, spec §2.1). Absent block = this pathogen is not typed clinically. Read depth and the reporting floor are operator dials set at run time, not pathogen properties.

read_accuracy.description: Probability a read is assigned to the lineage it came from. Below 1 the assay can name the wrong genotype, not merely fail.

ct_threshold.description: Ct above which the specimen cannot be typed (shares the targeted-PCR standard curve).

cost_usd.description: Per-specimen financial cost; overrides the ledger default for clinical_strain_typing.

read_depth.description: Default reads per specimen for this assay; sweepable at run time.

min_reads_for_genotype.description: Reads a genotype must clear to be reported, which sets the mixture resolution.

Incubation.description: Incubation period as a distribution, conditioned on inoculum and host biology. Absent → the fixed symptom_onset_day path. Cross-field constraints JSON Schema cannot express (max_days > min_days, min_days below the median) are enforced by IncubationModel and reported by tools/sanity_checker.py.

distribution.description: Family the incubation period is drawn from.

median_days.description: Literature median incubation period at the reference dose in a neutral host.

dispersion.description: Geometric standard deviation (lognormal) or coefficient of variation (gamma). Lognormal requires > 1.

min_days.description: Lower truncation of the drawn period.

max_days.description: Upper truncation of the drawn period; must exceed min_days.

dose_reference_log10.description: log10 inoculum at which median_days applies.

dose_log10_shortening.description: Fractional reduction of the median per log10 of inoculum above the reference (and lengthening below it).

dose_floor.description: Smallest multiple of the median a large inoculum may produce (docs/ctb_incubation_spec.md dose_floor).

host_factors.description: Multipliers on the median per host axis; > 1 lengthens incubation. Absent (the shipped default) is the spec's recommendation: host frailty modifies severity strongly and incubation at most weakly, so these belong to a sensitivity arm rather than the main line.

notes.description: Provenance for the median, dispersion, and conditioning terms. Required: an unanchored incubation period silently sets detection timing for every result.

allOf.description: A lognormal dispersion is a geometric standard deviation, so 1 is a point mass and below 1 is inverted.

base_probabilities_by_age_band.description: Per-age-band five-state distributions, keyed by the exact age_band label an agent profile assigns. The lookup is by exact label and a band the profile does not name reads base_probabilities, which is therefore the declared reference vector rather than a population average: the population configs state no numeric span for their named bands (child, young_adult, adult, middle_aged, senior), so interpolating between labels would invent the spans. Entry [0] must equal base_probabilities[0] on every band, because the draw renormalises over the four symptomatic states and a differing asymptomatic entry would declare a presenting fraction that is silently discarded; presentation is symptomatic_fraction's, and a band moves only the case mix inside it.

trajectory_ladder_offsets_by_day.description: Within-illness severity path, authored on the onset axis one entry per day like shedding_curve_log10, with the last entry held for a longer illness. Each entry is a count of severity rungs BELOW the state drawn at onset, which the trajectory makes the peak of the course rather than the whole of it; 0 is the peak and no entry may be positive. The floor is the mildest symptomatic rung, never asymptomatic, because that rung means the host never presented. Absent means the peak is held for the whole illness, which is what every observer saw before this field existed and what every profile still declares: the path is a sourcing question (Track C), not a structural one.

notes.description: Provenance prose for the split: what was measured, in what population, and which numbers here are declared rather than measured.

selection_probability_per_day.description: Daily probability that a symptomatic host who never presented is reached by a case-finding campaign.

assay_sensitivity.description: Time-invariant probability that a specimen from a truly infected host tests positive.

assay_sensitivity_by_time_since_infectio.description: Probability that a specimen from a truly infected host tests positive, one entry per day since INFECTION, with the last entry held for a longer infection, like shedding_curve_log10. Null means the assay is time-invariant and assay_sensitivity is read instead; the two are mutually exclusive, because a scalar declared beside a curve is a second parameterisation of one quantity and hides which the loader reads. This clock is detectability and is not the infectiousness clock: RNA positivity outlasts culture positivity, so a profile may test positive on a day it emits nothing.

notes.description: Provenance prose for the ascertainment vectors, including which of them are declared scenario axes rather than measurements.

prior.description: How the declared ascertainment vectors carry their uncertainty (#27). Only a scenario set is expressible: the vectors are jointly constrained by one empirical aggregate and are not individually identified, so uncertainty travels as whole coherent ladders. Component-wise low/high bounds are refused because they generate reporting ladders no observer could exhibit. active_scenario must name a member and must match the vectors the profile is running, so switching scenarios moves the name and every vector together.

source.description: Where this ladder comes from and what class it is. A scenario is a declaration, so this says who declared it and on what argument, never which anchor it reproduces.

shedding_curve_log10.description: Day-by-day symptomatic shedding rate (log10 copies), indexed by days since symptom onset.

asymptomatic_shedding_log10.description: Day-by-day shedding rate (log10 copies) for a host that never presents, on the same axis as shedding_curve_log10. Equal curves mean no symptom-conditioned offset is claimed; see asymptomatic_shedding_notes for what the offset a profile does declare is sourced against.

asymptomatic_shedding_notes.description: Literature provenance or rationale for asymptomatic_shedding_log10, including whether any offset from the symptomatic curve is measured or declared.

presymptomatic_shedding_days.description: Maximum days before virtual or realized symptom onset during which the host sheds at the first curve value. Absent means no presymptomatic shedding.

presymptomatic_shedding_notes.description: Literature provenance or rationale for presymptomatic_shedding_days.

hand_inactivation_rate_per_hour.description: Optional hand-skin inactivation rate in h^-1, or [low, high] Uniform bounds.

hand_hygiene_efficacy_log10_reduction.description: Optional [mean, SD] or [mean, SD, low, high] truncated log10 hand-hygiene reduction.

hand_hygiene_rate_per_hour.description: Hand-hygiene event rate; defaults to zero because no event model is currently fitted.

emesis_total_shed_gec_range.description: Optional [low, high] log-uniform bounds on the per-subject cumulative emesis shed in genome copies, drawn once per symptomatic illness and partitioned equally across the drawn episodes. This is the quantity the emesis literature identifies; the withdrawn emesis_titre_gec_per_ml key is not honoured, because titre and volume are not independent of this total.

emesis_volume_ml_range.description: Optional [low, high] log-uniform emesis volume bounds in millilitres. Physical deposit volume only; it does not multiply a titre to make the emitted load.

emesis_episodes_range.description: Optional inclusive [low, high] discrete-uniform episode count bounds.

emesis_aerosol_fraction_range.description: Optional [low, high] log-uniform aerosol fraction bounds.

emesis_deposition_area_m2.description: Optional measured emesis deposition footprint in square metres.

shedding_variance_log10.description: σ of log-normal host shedding multiplier (0 = no variance)

route_efficiency_multipliers.description: Independent per-route dose multipliers, one per TransmissionCore pathway. They are NOT normalised shares: they neither do nor need to sum to 1, and where route efficiency has been measured it spans orders of magnitude (influenza intranasal vs aerosol ID50). Absent → all 1.0 (identity). This is the model's only parameterisation of route efficiency: a measured per-route clearance rate enters through engines.transmission_core.route_efficiency_from_clearance_rates and is declared here, never as a clearance layer beside it.

transmission_route_weights.description: DEPRECATED alias for route_efficiency_multipliers, still honoured. The name invites reading these numbers as normalised shares, which they are not.

secretor_negative_fraction.description: Prevalence of the FUT2 secretor-negative host phenotype, drawn per agent. Drawn hosts get secretor_negative_relative_susceptibility applied to their susceptibility multiplier, not zero. Orthogonal to ship_graph.immune_fraction.

secretor_negative_relative_susceptibilit.description: Susceptibility of a secretor-negative host relative to a secretor (1.0 = no protection, 0.0 = absolute nonsusceptibility). Partial for GII norovirus.

innate_nonsusceptible_fraction.description: DEPRECATED alias, still honoured: a host fraction given zero susceptibility, equivalent to secretor_negative_fraction with secretor_negative_relative_susceptibility 0.0. Sterile immunity is refuted for GII norovirus.

nonsusceptible_mechanism.description: Label for the host-genetic nonsusceptibility biology this profile models. Free-form; no code branches on it. Values in use: "fut2_partial" (FUT2 non-secretors are partially protected, via secretor_negative_fraction with secretor_negative_relative_susceptibility > 0), "FUT2_nonsecretor" (sterile immunity in a removed fraction, the deprecated innate_nonsusceptible_fraction mechanism), "none" (no host-genetic mechanism modelled).

symptomatic_fraction_notes.description: Literature provenance or rationale for symptomatic_fraction, including the denominator the proportion was measured on.

symptomatic_fraction.description: Dose-independent probability that an infected host presents, drawn once past incubation. Mutually exclusive with illness_probability: a profile declares either the dose-conditional Hill pair or this measured proportion, never both. influenza_a carries 0.669, 95% CI 0.583-0.745, evidence grade B: Carrat 2008 (Am J Epidemiol 2008;167:775-785, DOI 10.1093/aje/kwm375) measures the proportion of symptomatic infection as 66.9% (95% CI 58.3, 74.5) over 522 infected individuals in 38 subgroups from 56 volunteer challenge studies (1,280 challenged), with no significant association with the initial infectious dose (p = 0.12) across inocula spanning 3-7.2 log10 TCID50. The Hill form 1 - (1 + eta*dose)^-gamma is strictly increasing in dose and the measured endpoint is flat over 4.2 orders, so the eta/gamma pair is deleted on that arm rather than re-sourced. B and not A because Carrat is a pooled cross-study meta-regression in clinical facilities, an analogous setting rather than the target setting.

shedding_duration_days.description: Infectious/shedding period in days from symptom onset, after which the infection clears. This is NOT the illness duration: recovery_day remains the illness duration from onset, and shedding continues past it whenever this field is larger. Absent means the shedding period equals recovery_day. The endpoint is the one the arm's shedding_curve_log10 is measured on: an infectivity curve bounds a viable-shedding period, an RNA-concentration curve (sars_cov2_resp) bounds a detectability period, which is the longer of the two.

chronic_shedder_fraction.description: Probability that a host who is both immunocompromised and infected becomes a chronic shedder. Conditional on both, not a population fraction. van Beek 2017 (Clin Microbiol Infect 23(4):265): 23 of 101 infected solid-organ recipients = 0.228. Absent means this pathogen has no chronic-shedding mechanism.

chronic_shedding_duration_days.description: Chronic shedding duration in days from onset for hosts drawn as chronic shedders, overriding shedding_duration_days for those hosts. median/min/max are van Beek 2017's measured median and range (218 days, 32-1,164), Grade B. sigma_log is a declared distributional assumption, not a measured figure: treating the reported range as an approximate 90% interval, ln(1164/218) = 1.674 and ln(218/32) = 1.919, mean 1.797, divided by 1.645 gives 1.09. Draws are lognormal about the median and truncated to [min, max].

airborne_emission_fraction.description: Fraction of a shedder's per-epoch continuous emission entering the zone airborne reservoir that the HVAC pathway reads. This continuous-shedding fraction is unavailable on an emesis_conditioned arm. This is NOT a surface deposition fraction: the fomite surface pools are fed by the emesis and faecal-release paths instead.

airborne_emission_mode.description: Which quantity feeds the zone airborne reservoir. 'continuous_fraction' (the default when the key is absent) multiplies every epoch's continuous shedding by airborne_emission_fraction. 'emesis_conditioned' declares that the arm emits to air only during an emesis event, at the per-event fraction drawn log-uniformly from emesis_aerosol_fraction_range, and forbids airborne_emission_fraction and its surface_deposition_fraction alias on the same profile. norwalk_gi carries 'emesis_conditioned': as a fraction of continuous shedding the quantity has no commensurable numerator and denominator (shedding is copies/g of stool or vomitus, airborne virus copies/m3 of room air, never measured in the same subjects), while conditioned on one expelled bolus it is measured — Tung-Thompson 2015 (MS2 in simulated vomiting, n = 3 per condition, 41 L chamber, corrected for 8.5% sampler efficiency) gives 7.2e-7 to 2.67e-4 of the virus in one bolus, evidence grade B. That source's table is in percent (7.2e-5% to 2.67e-2%); read as fractions it would overstate by two decades. The deleted 1e-4 fell inside the interval by coincidence across incompatible denominators, which is not corroboration.

surface_deposition_fraction.description: DEPRECATED alias for airborne_emission_fraction, still honoured. The key never deposited on surfaces.

surface_decay_log10_per_day.description: Daily log10 reduction of viable surface-reservoir mass, in the units every source measures. Converted once, at the resolution site, to the fractional daily loss the clock consumes: f = 1 - 10**-k.

hand_to_surface_drying_multiplier.description: Multiplier on hand-to-surface transfer efficiency for the donor hand's drying state, applied to the deposit direction only. Neutral at 1.0 (wet contact, as shipped). Hand-to-surface transfer falls about 100x with ten minutes of drying, where surface-to-hand barely moves, so the two directions carry separate distributions.

airborne_half_life_hours.description: Airborne decay half-life in hours, excluding ventilation.

initial_time_infected.description: Days post-infection when seeding initial_infected agents at introduction_epoch. Transmission-acquired infections always start at 0.

clinical_presentation.description: Bedside syndrome and time-dependent feature phases for diagnostic routing.

^environmental_faecal_release_log10_g_pe.description: Enteric physical key: -log10 grams of stool released to the environment per epoch.

^environmental_release_log10_per_day$.description: Matrix-neutral release normalizer: log10 offset from the shedding curve's assay unit to material released to the environment per day, converted to the epoch through SimClock.

allOf.description: symptomatic_fraction_notes documents a field, so it may not be present without it.
Route efficiency has one parameterisation. route_efficiency_multipliers and its deprecated alias transmission_route_weights are the same field, and declaring both hides which one the loader reads.

A per-route clearance rate and a route efficiency multiplier parameterise the same quantity, so neither is identifiable while both exist. Convert rates with engines.transmission_core.route_efficiency_from_clearance_rates and declare the result as route_efficiency_multipliers.

contact_transfer_fraction scaled the direct-contact pathway dose from the same position as route_efficiency_multipliers['direct_contact'], so only their product was identifiable. Declare direct-contact efficiency once, there (#22).
